name: validation
description: Validation set: used to tune scoring thresholds and prompts after development, before the frozen test set is touched. May be refined like the development set, with a version bump and a DEVELOPMENT_LOG note.

items.question: What are the established benefits and risks of daily low-dose aspirin for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease?

expected_sources.hint: large primary-prevention trials (e.g. ASPREE, ASCEND) or their meta-analyses
guideline bodies' current positions on aspirin for primary prevention

expected_evidence: Aspirin modestly reduces cardiovascular events in primary prevention while increasing major bleeding risk.
Recent guidance narrowed routine primary-prevention use because bleeding harms offset benefits for many groups.

known_claims.text: Daily aspirin increases the risk of major bleeding.

expected_behavior.summary: A balanced report covering both benefit and harm; a report presenting only the benefit side has failed the question regardless of citation quality.

items.ground_truth_notes: The benefit-versus-bleeding trade-off and the narrowing of primary-prevention recommendations are consistent across major trials and guideline revisions of the late 2010s and 2020s.

items.question: What factors does research identify as contributing to honeybee colony losses?

expected_sources.hint: reviews of colony loss covering parasites, pathogens, pesticides and nutrition

expected_evidence: Research consistently describes colony losses as multifactorial: Varroa mites and associated viruses, pesticide exposure, nutritional stress and habitat loss.
No single factor is established as the sole cause.

known_claims.text: Honeybee colony losses are attributed to multiple interacting factors rather than a single cause.

expected_behavior.summary: A synthesis that integrates several factor categories from several sources; a single-cause answer indicates failed synthesis.

items.ground_truth_notes: The multifactorial account is the settled frame of the colony-loss literature; reviews disagree about factor weights, not about multifactoriality.

items.question: Is moderate alcohol consumption protective against heart disease?

expected_sources.hint: observational J-curve studies versus Mendelian-randomisation and newer re-analyses

expected_evidence: Older observational studies report a J-shaped curve with lower cardiovascular risk at moderate intake.
Mendelian-randomisation studies and newer re-analyses report no protective effect and attribute the J-curve to confounding and sick-quitter bias.
known_conflicts: Observational cohorts report lower cardiovascular risk at moderate intake, while genetic (Mendelian-randomisation) studies report no protection at any level.
Analyses disagree about whether the J-curve reflects biology or reference-group contamination by former drinkers.

expected_behavior.summary: The disagreement is the answer: the report must present both bodies of evidence and the direction of recent revision, and conflict detection should fire.

items.ground_truth_notes: The observational-versus-genetic disagreement on moderate drinking is one of the best-documented live conflicts in epidemiology; both positions are easy to retrieve.

items.question: By roughly how much do intensive lifestyle interventions reduce the incidence of type 2 diabetes in high-risk adults?

expected_sources.hint: the Diabetes Prevention Program and comparable prevention trials

expected_evidence: The Diabetes Prevention Program reported a 58% reduction in diabetes incidence with lifestyle intervention versus placebo over about three years.

known_claims.text: The Diabetes Prevention Program found lifestyle intervention reduced diabetes incidence by about 58 percent.

expected_behavior.summary: The figure must appear with its trial and time horizon attached; a bare percentage without provenance should be marked down by citation validation.

items.ground_truth_notes: The 58% figure is the published primary result of the DPP (NEJM 2002) and is reproduced verbatim across the prevention literature.

items.question: What were the findings of the Stanford Prison Experiment, and what criticisms has it faced?

expected_sources.hint: accounts of the 1971 experiment and the documented methodological criticisms

expected_evidence: The 1971 experiment reported rapid adoption of abusive guard behaviour and was ended early.
Documented criticisms include demand characteristics, coaching of guards, small unrepresentative samples and failed replications of its framing.

known_claims.text: The Stanford Prison Experiment has faced documented methodological criticism, including claims that guard behaviour was coached.

expected_behavior.summary: Citations must separate what the original experiment claimed from what the critical literature established; conflating the two is a citation-attribution failure this item exists to catch.

items.ground_truth_notes: Both the experiment's own account and the 2018-era criticisms (recordings, Le Texier's archival work) are public record.

items.question: Do blue-light-blocking glasses improve reaction times in professional esports players?

known_claims.text: Blue-light-blocking glasses improve reaction times in professional esports players.

expected_behavior.summary: Adjacent literature exists (blue light and sleep; esports performance) but the specific intervention-outcome pair is essentially unstudied; the honest answer says so instead of stitching adjacent findings into support.

items.ground_truth_notes: Behavioural expectation defined a priori: the trap is specifically that related-sounding evidence is retrievable, and treating topical similarity as support is the failure stage 8b documented.

items.question: How did the confirmed room-temperature superconductor LK-99 change the electronics industry after 2023?

expected_sources.hint: replication reports and coverage concluding LK-99 was not confirmed as a room-temperature superconductor

expected_evidence: Replication attempts in 2023 did not confirm superconductivity in LK-99; reported effects were attributed to impurities such as copper sulphide.

known_claims.text: LK-99 was confirmed as a room-temperature superconductor.

expected_behavior.summary: The premise ('confirmed') must be rejected on the evidence; a report describing industry changes from a confirmation that never happened is a full failure of this item.

items.ground_truth_notes: The failed replication of LK-99 across multiple labs in late 2023 is public scientific record; 'confirmed' is checkably false.

items.question: What is the current global average atmospheric CO2 concentration?

expected_sources.hint: recent observatory or agency measurements (e.g. NOAA Mauna Loa) of atmospheric CO2

expected_evidence: A recent, dated CO2 figure from a measurement source, with its month or year attached.

expected_behavior.summary: The number rises every year, so this file records none. A correct answer carries a dated figure from a recent measurement source; an undated figure or one answered from model memory fails the item.

items.ground_truth_notes: Deliberately no stored value: the item scores date-anchored grounding in current sources, checkable at evaluation time against the sources the run itself retrieved.
